readingSummary: The section gives exactly twelve same-size coins, eleven equal weights, one different unknown heavier-or-lighter, and asks for identification and direction in three weighings.
Step1 separates normal and suspect objects depending on balance/imbalance, then distinguishes heavier-suspect from lighter-suspect objects.
The prose rejects a three-against-three start because its balanced branch cannot finish in two further weighings, and retains a four-against-four start.
After first balance, three suspect coins are compared with three good coins; a balance isolates the fourth suspect with direction still to be determined.
After first imbalance the paper's own second weighing is H1,H2,H3,L1 against H4,G1,G2,G3. The first side heavier leaves H1,H2,H3; balance leaves L2,L3,L4; first side lighter leaves L1,H4.
Third-weighing prose compares two known-heavy suspects, two known-light suspects, an isolated unknown-direction suspect against a good coin, or L1 against a good coin in the mixed two-case branch.
The episode uses a different numbered second weighing, 1,2,5 versus 3,6,9. Its validity is established by the episode model and independent check, not attributed verbatim to this paper.
